title: Chloroform-Methanol Protein Extraction with Zymolyase Treatment for Yeast
author: Jennifer Gin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bhptj5nn
materials: Chemicals to prepare: • Prepare 100 millimolar (mM), Tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP) solution by dissolving 28.7 mg, TCEP in 1 mL, 100mM Ammonium Bicarbonate • Prepare 200 millimolar (mM), Iodoacetamide (IAA) solution by dissolving 36.8 mg, Iodoacetamide in 1 mL, 100mM Ammonium Bicarbonate •Prepare 1 mg/mL, Trypsin by adding 1 mL, 1mM HCl to 1 mg, Trypsin Store TCEP, IAA, and Trypsin in -20C. IAA is light sensitive. Store in amber tube (Fisher Scientific, Cat.#05-402-31).
Carefully pipet out clear liquid sample into plastic autosampler vials (ThermoFisherScientific, Cat.#03-060-016) or a 96-well plate (BIO-RAD, Cat.#HSP9601).

steps.title: Thaw cells at room temperature
steps.instruction: Thaw the yeast cell pellet at room temperature; if cells are taken directly from an active culture, skip this step.

steps.title: Prepare Zymolyase digestion buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1.822 g sorbitol and 0.292 g ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) in 10 mL deionized water to make Zymolyase buffer.

steps.title: Add Zymolyase to buffer and resuspend cells
steps.instruction: Add 1.5 µL (7.5 U) Zymolyase to 200 µL of the prepared Zymolyase buffer, then resuspend the thawed cells in this mixture.

steps.title: Incubate for cell wall digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate the suspension in a 37 °C water bath (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Cat.#TSGP2S) for 10 minutes to digest the cell walls.

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4000 rpm, 25 °C for 1 minute, then carefully remove and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Transfer cell pellet to PCR tubes
steps.instruction: Transfer 2–4 OD·mL of the resulting cell pellet to 8‑strip PCR tubes (Axygen, Cat.#14‑222‑251) or a 96‑well PCR plate (ThermoFisher, Cat.#AB0600); a strip filled 30–40 % full corresponds to ~10–20 OD·mL.

steps.title: Add methanol and resuspend
steps.instruction: Add 80 µL LC‑MS grade methanol (VWR Scientific, Cat.#BJLC230‑2.5) to each tube and pipet to resuspend the pellet thoroughly.

steps.title: Add chloroform and mix
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL chloroform (Sigma‑Aldrich, Cat.#34854) to each tube, then pipet/vortex to mix. Perform this step in a fume hood.

steps.title: Add water and mix
steps.instruction: Add 60 µL LC‑MS grade water (VWR Scientific, Cat.#BJLC365‑2.5) and pipet/vortex to mix.

steps.title: Centrifuge to separate phases
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4000 rpm, 25 °C for 1 minute.

steps.title: Remove top aqueous layer
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, carefully remove the upper layer (methanol + water) without disturbing the interphase.

steps.title: Add methanol to pellet
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL methanol; break up the protein pellet by piercing it with the pipette tip and direct the methanol to the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet protein
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4000 rpm, 25 °C for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Discard organic solvents
steps.instruction: Carefully discard the supernatant (methanol + chloroform) into an appropriate halogenated‑solvent waste container.

steps.title: Air‑dry protein pellet
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet for 5 minutes in a fume hood (do not exceed 45 minutes, otherwise the pellet becomes difficult to resuspend).

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in ammonium bicarbonate
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in 60 µL 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate containing 20 % methanol. The suspension will appear cloudy.

steps.title: Store samples at –20 °C
steps.instruction: Store the resuspended protein samples at –20 °C until ready for protein quantitation.

steps.title: Dilute samples ten‑fold with water
steps.instruction: In a new PCR tube or well, add 5 µL of the protein sample to 45 µL deionized water, mix well; this creates a 10‑fold dilution.

steps.title: Load standards and samples onto assay plate
steps.instruction: Transfer 2 replicates of each of the following into a Corning 96‑well black polystyrene microplate (Fisher Scientific, Cat.#07‑200‑590): 5 µL water (blank), 5 µL Pierce BSA standard (ThermoFisher, Cat.#23208), and 5 µL of each diluted sample.

steps.title: Add Reagent A and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL Bio‑Rad DC Protein Assay Reagent A (Bio‑rad Laboratories, Cat.#500‑0113) to each well and incubate for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add Reagent B and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL Bio‑Rad DC Protein Assay Reagent B (Bio‑rad Laboratories, Cat.#500‑0114) to each well and incubate for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Measure absorbance at 280 nm
steps.instruction: Read the plate in a microplate reader at 280 nm and calculate protein concentrations using the standard curve.

steps.title: Dilute proteins to 2.4 µg/µL in AMBIC
steps.instruction: Adjust each protein sample to a concentration of 2.4 µg/µL using 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate (AMBIC); mix well before further processing.

steps.title: Prepare reduction/alkylation/trypsin mix
steps.instruction:
For a 50 µL final digestion volume, add the following (choose the appropriate set based on available protein):
• Option A (2.4 µg/µL protein): 41.67 µL protein, 2.5 µL 100 mM TCEP, 2.5 µL 200 mM IAA, 2 µL trypsin (1 mg/mL, 1:50 enzyme:protein), then add AMBIC to 50 µL total.
• Option B (lower protein, 1 µg/µL): 20.83 µL protein, 2.5 µL 100 mM TCEP, 2.5 µL 200 mM IAA, 1 µL trypsin (1 mg/mL), then add AMBIC to 50 µL total.
Final concentrations: 2 µg/µL protein, 5 mM TCEP, 10 mM IAA, trypsin at 1:50 (w/w).

steps.title: Incubate digestion at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the digestion mixture at 37 °C for 4 – 16 hours.

steps.title: Centrifuge digests
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4000 rpm, 4 °C for 15 minutes to pellet any insoluble material.

steps.title: Store digests at –20 °C
steps.instruction: Store the cleared digests at –20 °C until ready for LC‑MS/MS analysis.
